newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso holds weak early levels to end soft.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso holds weak early levels to end soft.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker on Friday after drifting sideways for most of the session following early corporate demand to cover dollar positions, traders said.
"There was some month-end dollar buying early on, but on the whole it was a quiet session," traders said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso MXAAA and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.4 and 1.5 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8880/7.8930 and 7.8830/7.8870 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 1.7 centavos weaker at 7.8730/7.8780.
Traders said the session was quiet following the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
Dealers said they expected the peso to weaken against the dollar during the first half of December due to a seasonal spike in inflation, which could pare real interest rates.
They said the peso could be under further pressure from year-end demand from corporations and banks to close dollar positions.
The 48-hour peso closed the week 1.3 centavos below last week, but 8.7 centavos firmer than the close of October.
